name: CalibrationLiftedFace
description: A plain plate whose top face is then pushed 2 mm further up. The instrument for `move_face`, and the only calibration fixture here whose true answer is exact rather than estimated: a rectangular prism's cap keeps its area as it translates, so the solid gains exactly area times distance, 32 cm^2 x 0.2 cm = 6.4 cm^3, and the simulator's dot product says the same thing for the same reason. That makes this a prediction Inventor can break rather than a number to be measured and copied down. It matters because the assumption the estimate rests on -- that the moved face keeps its area -- is true here and is not true of a face bounded by a fillet or a draft, so a run that agrees puts a number on the arithmetic and says nothing yet about the harder case. The distance is a parameter, deliberately: this operation exists for imported geometry, which has no parameters to drive, and the one thing a live run can still confirm is that the expression reaches Inventor's own dimension on a part built here.

parameters.name: lift
parameters.comment: how much taller the plate becomes; 80 x 40 x 2 mm is 6.4 cm^3
